name: MonarchEditorToolbar
title: EditorToolbar
wrapsNative: Toggle with .toggleStyle(.monarchButton) and Button per tool, Menu with a Picker for the text style, alert with a TextField for links, in a horizontal ScrollView; placed with ToolbarItemGroup(placement: .keyboard)
summary: A formatting toolbar for a text editor: undo and redo, a text style menu, inline styles, lists, quotes, code and links, plus product controls.
whenToUse: Above the keyboard or above an editor where people format rich text, such as notes, comments or documents.
whenNotToUse: Not for a plain text field (no formatting) and not for the actions of a screen (use the navigation bar's toolbar items).
api: init(groups: [[MonarchEditorTool]] = MonarchEditorTool.defaultGroups, active: Set<MonarchEditorTool> = [], disabled: Set<MonarchEditorTool> = [], labels: MonarchEditorToolbarLabels = MonarchEditorToolbarLabels(), onLink: (@MainActor (URL?) -> Void)? = nil, action: @escaping @MainActor (MonarchEditorTool) -> Void)

enum MonarchEditorTool: Hashable { case undo, redo, paragraph, heading(Int), bold, italic, strikethrough, code, link, bulletList, orderedList, taskList, blockquote, codeBlock, custom(id: String, title: String, systemImage: String); static let defaultGroups: [[MonarchEditorTool]]; static let inlineGroups: [[MonarchEditorTool]] }

struct MonarchEditorToolbarLabels { init(toolbar: String? = nil, tools: [MonarchEditorTool: String] = [:], textStyle: String? = nil, linkTitle: String? = nil, linkAddress: String? = nil, linkApply: String? = nil, linkRemove: String? = nil, linkCancel: String? = nil, linkHelp: String? = nil) }

options.name: groups
options.description: The tools in groups separated by dividers. Neighbouring paragraph and heading tools become one text style menu. MonarchEditorTool.inlineGroups gives inline formatting only.

options.name: active
options.description: The formats that are on at the caret or selection, and the current text style. The app's editor works these out.

options.name: disabled
options.description: Tools that cannot be used now, such as undo with nothing to undo.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the toolbar name, every tool name (by tool), the text style menu and the link form.

options.name: onLink
options.description: Makes the link tool open a form for the address. Receives a safe URL to apply, or nil when Remove link is pressed. Without it, the link tool goes to action.

options.name: action
options.description: Runs when a tool is pressed or a text style is chosen. The app applies it to its editor.

states.name: on
states.description: A toggle whose format is active has the accent fill and border of the Monarch toggle button style.

states.name: disabled tool
states.description: Drawn in the disabled colours and cannot be pressed.

states.name: link form
states.description: A system alert with an address field, Apply (disabled until the address is valid), Remove link when a link is active, and Cancel.

states.name: disabled
states.description: With .disabled(true) every control is disabled, for example while the editor loads.

appearance: Small ghost Monarch buttons and toggle buttons with SF Symbols, separated by thin dividers in the subtle border role, in a row that scrolls sideways. All colours are theme roles, so dark and high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web toolbar drives a Tiptap editor directly. iOS has no Monarch rich text editor yet, so this toolbar is editor-agnostic: the app passes which formats are on and applies what is pressed (for example to an AttributedString in its own editor). Headings are one text style menu instead of a button per level, to fit a phone. The link popover is a system alert with a text field. The web's arrow-key roving focus and keyboard shortcut hints are not offered; iOS moves through the controls with VoiceOver and Full Keyboard Access, and hardware shortcuts belong to the app's text view.
accessibility: The toolbar is a container named "Formatting".
Format tools are standard toggles with the Monarch toggle button style, so VoiceOver reads their name and on or off value; the on state is also a filled surface.
Undo, redo and product tools are standard buttons named by their title.
The text style menu is a standard menu named "Text style" whose value is the current style; its entries are a picker with a check mark on the current one.
Group dividers are hidden from VoiceOver.
Every control has a 44-point touch target; icons have spoken names through their Label titles.
edgeCases: Empty groups are dropped, so two dividers never meet.
Heading levels outside 1 through 6 use the level 6 symbol.
A link typed as a bare domain becomes https; an email becomes mailto; javascript, data and other schemes are refused.

examples.title: Every control
examples.setupTemplate:
@Environment(\.monarchTheme) private var theme
@State private var active: Set<MonarchEditorTool> = [.heading({{activeHeading}})]
examples.setup:
@Environment(\.monarchTheme) private var theme
@State private var active: Set<MonarchEditorTool> = [.heading(2)]

examples.title: Inline tools above the keyboard

parityExceptions.reason: The web toolbar shows every tool in one row at its width; on iPhone the toolbar is a horizontally scrolling row of 44 pt buttons (the usual keyboard-accessory pattern), so the tools after the first seven are reached by scrolling.
